paras: The beating of a Black youth near St. Asaph, Virginia, took place on August 22, 1905, when Mr. McDonald and other residents of Alexandria county chased down four 'colored youths' and one who resisted was badly beaten in the face. All four were jailed on a charge of abusive language and disorderly conduct, and a rumor that a criminal assault had been attempted was denied at the courthouse.

According to the account given to the Washington Evening Star's Alexandria correspondent, several Black men went to McDonald's house near St. Asaph while he was away and demanded something to eat from his wife. The same account, attributed only to 'it is stated', said they became 'very threatening and abusive' and that Mrs. McDonald barred the doors against them.

McDonald and others answered her alarm, and four of the suspects were caught near Four-Mile Run after what the paper called a long chase. One of the four, who resisted, was badly beaten in the face, and several of his teeth were knocked out; the report does not say who struck him. The youths were taken to the county courthouse on Fort Meyer Heights and placed in jail.

Justice Burrell was notified and was to give the prisoners a hearing on the afternoon of August 23. The incident gave rise to a report in Alexandria that a criminal assault had been attempted, but officials at the courthouse said that morning that no such charge had been lodged. No report of the hearing's outcome, or of any action against those who beat the youth, appears in the coverage.

The episode is known from a single paragraph in the Evening Star's 'Alexandria Affairs' column of August 23, headed 'Colored Youths Arrested' and placed between a report on the condition of the Braddock House and local death notices. The item treated the arrests as the news, mentioned the beating in one sentence without comment, and gave the household's version of the encounter as hearsay. Its closing sentence corrected the circulating rumor of an attempted criminal assault; no Black-press coverage of the episode was found.

reader.title: Beating of a Black youth during a chase near St. Asaph, Virginia
bases: According to the only report, private citizens who answered Mrs. McDonald's alarm chased four Black youths, and one who resisted was badly beaten in the face before all were jailed (A1).
One white-press item, a correspondent's paragraph attributed to 'it is stated', is the only report found; no Black-press coverage or follow-up surfaced (A1).
